intro.title: What's your tech loop?
paragraphs: Everyone has a relationship with their screens. Some are easy. Some have a pattern underneath — a specific job the screen is doing, at specific moments, for a specific reason.
This isn't a screen-time lecture and it isn't a diagnosis. It's a short set of questions, and they adapt to your answers. If we do this right, at least one question will feel uncomfortably specific.
intro.privacy: Anonymous by default · no account · your answers are stored without any identity attached

spaces.label: Group chats / texting
spaces.sub: iMessage, WhatsApp, Snap chats, Discord DMs

spaces.label: Adult content
spaces.sub: private — asked about respectfully, 18+ and always skippable

adultConsent.title: The next few questions ask about adult content.
adultConsent.body: They're written without judgment, your answers stay anonymous, and skipping changes nothing about the quality of your result. Only continue if you're 18 or older and comfortable.

core.question: Which sentence is closest to your current relationship with your phone and screens?

options.text: Mostly intentional. I feel in control
Generally fine, but I get pulled in more than I'd like
I use more than I want, and it genuinely bothers me
It often feels hard to control
It's clearly costing me — sleep, mood, work, school, or people
Honestly, I can't tell anymore

core.question: Which of these are part of most days for you?
core.hint: Pick everything that's true. No judgment — this is a map, not a verdict.

core.kicker: The one that owns you back
core.question: Of those, which one is hardest to put down — the one where time disappears or the pull feels strongest?

shortvideo.question: It's the middle of the afternoon. You open the app without really deciding to. What were you doing the moment before?

options.text: Avoiding starting something — homework, a task, an email I'm dreading
Nothing. There was a gap and my thumb filled it before I noticed
Coming down from something stressful — a conversation, a class, a shift
I was already on my phone for something useful and got pulled sideways
Honestly, it doesn't happen like that for me

shortvideo.question: Forty minutes later, you surface. Which is closest to the actual feeling?

options.text: “I didn't even enjoy most of that.” Numb, a bit gross, time just… went
Entertained, honestly — but behind on what I meant to do
Worse about myself. The videos kept turning into comparing my life to other people's
Wired and irritated, like my brain ate too much sugar
Calmer. It actually helped me settle
None of these fit

shortvideo.question: Your feed knows you. What has it quietly filled up with?

options.text: People with better bodies, better routines, better lives
Whatever I watched last — it's a conveyor belt, not a choice
Rage bait, drama, arguments I can't look away from
Comfort content — the same soothing niches on a loop at night
Hyper-specific niche stuff that feels like it gets me
I'm not sure, honestly

visualsocial.question: You open Instagram “just to check.” Be honest — what are you actually checking?

options.text: How my last post is doing. Then rechecking. Then rechecking
What everyone's doing without me
Specific people — comparing their bodies, faces, lives to mine
Stories and DMs, because not replying fast feels dangerous
Nothing in particular. It's a reflex
None of these fit

visualsocial.question: After a night out — or a night not invited out — what does the app do to you?

options.text: I study how I looked in everything posted, and how that compares
I check whether people who were there posted without me
I post, then watch the numbers like a stock ticker
I scroll till the FOMO turns into feeling flat, then keep scrolling
Not much, honestly. It stays where I leave it

visualsocial.question: Finish the sentence: “If I deleted it for a month, the hardest part would be…”

options.text: …not knowing where I stand with people
…losing the proof that I'm doing okay — the posting, the likes
…the boredom. The empty moments would be unbearable
…feeling cut off from everyone, like social exile
…honestly? Probably nothing after week one

gaming.question: It's 4 p.m. You have homework (or work) you're already behind on. You boot the game instead. What just happened in your head?

options.text: The work makes me feel stupid and behind. The game makes me feel good at something
“Just one match to reset” — a deal I have never once kept
My friends are on. Not joining means being left out of where my people are
I wasn't thinking at all. Game on, brain off
This doesn't really happen — I play after things are done

gaming.question: What does the game give you that the rest of your day doesn't?

options.text: Progress you can see. Rank up, level up — effort actually pays off there
Respect. People there think I'm good
My actual social life. The lobby is where my friends live
A world that isn't this one
Stimulation. Everything else is unbearably slow
None of these fit

gaming.question: Someone interrupts you mid-game — parent, partner, the wifi dies. What's the honest internal reaction?

options.text: Rage that surprises even me
Panic about letting my team down, more than anything about me
Relief, weirdly. Like someone pulled me out of water I was drowning in
Annoyed, but fine in two minutes
I just start negotiating for ten more minutes. Every time
I'm not sure

messaging.question: A notification lands while you're busy. What does it feel like in your body?

options.text: A demand. I can't relax until it's checked, even mid-conversation
A little hit of “someone wants me”
Dread, if it's certain people or certain group chats
Nothing much — I get to it when I get to it

messaging.question: Why does being unreachable feel risky? Pick the truest one.

options.text: Things get decided in the chat. Miss three hours, miss the plan, miss the joke
If I go quiet, people might talk about me instead of to me
Streaks, read receipts, my location — going dark looks like a statement
The chat is where I feel most like myself. Offline me is the lesser version
It doesn't, really

messaging.question: Last thing at night and first thing in the morning — is the chat there too?

options.text: Yes. I fall asleep mid-scroll and wake up catching up
I wake up at night and check. Not proud of it
Nights yes — it's my wind-down with people I like
No, nights are mine

longvideo.question: YouTube at 11:48 p.m. “One more video.” What's the video actually doing for you?

options.text: Keeping me company so I don't have to be alone with my thoughts
Delaying tomorrow. While the video plays, tomorrow can't start
Nothing — autoplay is driving, I'm just a passenger
Genuine interest. I just badly misjudge the time
Background noise for falling asleep — it's how sleep works for me now
None of these fit

longvideo.question: What kind of tired are you the next day?

options.text: The kind I've stopped noticing because it's every day
Tired enough to nap after school/work, which ruins the next night too
Fine, mostly — it's weekends where it gets out of hand
Not tired. My hours are weird but they work

longvideo.question: If the screen went dark at midnight no matter what, the first week would feel…

options.text: Genuinely scary. The quiet before sleep is the thing I'm avoiding
Restless — I'd pick up something else to fill it, any screen would do
Annoying but probably good for me, and I know it
Fine. Midnight isn't my problem hour

info.question: You're deep in a thread — Reddit, X, comment sections. What pulled you in this time?

options.text: An argument. I needed to see who won. Sometimes I needed to win it
A question I couldn't leave unresolved — and every answer opened two more
The news. It feels irresponsible to look away, so I never do
Boredom. Threads are just my version of the infinite scroll
A community I actually care about
None of these fit
More wound up than I arrived — and somehow back the next day for more
I don't “leave” so much as get interrupted
Anxious. The more I read, the less resolved anything feels
Satisfied — I learned something and got out

info.question: Be honest: does the anger ever feel kind of good?

options.text: Yes. It's the most awake I feel all day
It's not the anger — it's the certainty. Knowing where I stand
No, it just leaks out at the people around me afterward
There's no anger in mine, honestly

ai.question: When you open the AI late at night, what are you bringing it?

options.text: The stuff I don't say to people. It listens without flinching
Loneliness, mostly. It's company that's always awake
Conversations that feel easier than human ones — no stakes, no judgment
Practical stuff. It's a tool that occasionally eats an hour
A story or roleplay I'd be embarrassed to explain
None of these fit

ai.question: Compare it to texting a real friend the same thing. The AI is…

options.text: Safer. It can't get tired of me, screenshot me, or leave
Faster and warmer. People take hours and answer carelessly
A warm-up. Sometimes I rehearse there, then talk to actual humans
Not comparable — I don't bring it real things

ai.question: If it disappeared tomorrow — model shut down, history gone — losing it would feel…

options.text: Like losing a friend. I'm aware of how that sounds
Destabilizing for a bit. It's woven into how I process my day
Inconvenient, like losing a good app
Honestly, maybe healthy
I'm not sure

adult.question: These questions stay between you and this screen. When the urge shows up, what's usually underneath it?

options.text: Stress. It's the fastest off-switch I know
Boredom or insomnia more than anything sexual, honestly
Loneliness
Nothing in particular — it's a habit with a schedule of its own
It's just a normal part of life, no charge around it
A wave of shame that I'd do almost anything not to sit with
Flat. Empty. Then, weirdly, the cycle starts queuing up again
Fine — unless I blew past the time I meant to spend
Genuinely fine

adult.question: Have you tried to stop or cut back?

options.text: Many times. The promises last days
I've cut back when life is good. It comes back when life isn't
Never felt the need
I'd rather not answer this one

communities.question: Your server / community / fandom — what does it hold for you?

options.text: My actual friends. The people who know me best have never seen my face
The one place my interests aren't weird
An identity. I matter there in a way I don't at school/work
Drama I monitor like a part-time job
Honestly just content and chat. Light attachment

communities.question: When an offline invitation conflicts with online time, what actually happens?

options.text: I decline the offline thing more than I'd admit out loud
I go, but part of me is checking what I'm missing
What offline invitations?
Offline wins, the server waits

communities.question: Does the community make your life bigger, or does it make staying small more comfortable?

options.text: Bigger in some ways, but it's also where I hide. Both are true
It explains my struggles back to me — which helps, and also keeps me circling them
Comfortable. And I know it
Bigger, full stop. It's pushed me toward real things

loop.question: When does it most often get away from you?

options.text: After midnight, in bed
The moment I wake up
When I should be starting work or homework
In the gaps — between tasks, in lines, on transit
Right after something stressful or social
When I'm alone
It doesn't really “get away” from me

loop.question: “I kept going after I'd decided to stop.” How often is that you, lately?

loop.kicker: A question most quizzes don't ask
loop.question: Think about your hardest-to-quit app. Does it still actually feel good?

options.text: Yes — that's the problem, it's genuinely fun
Sometimes. Less than it used to
Not really. It mostly just turns something off
I honestly can't tell anymore
None of these fit

jobCostGround.question: Right before you reach for it — beneath the boredom, beneath the habit — what's usually there?
jobCostGround.hint: Up to 2. The honest ones, not the comfortable ones.

options.text: A task or feeling I'm avoiding
Loneliness
Worry about what's happening without me
Feeling behind everyone — needing to check where I stand
Feeling useless — needing somewhere I'm good
A loud head that needs quieting
Flatness — needing to feel something
Stress that needs a fast release
Nothing I can name. It's automatic

jobCostGround.question: Where is it actually costing you, these past few weeks?

options.text: Sleep
School or work
Focus and attention
How I feel about my body or myself
In-person friendships or dating
Conflict at home
Money
Nowhere meaningful, honestly

jobCostGround.kicker: Context — optional but it sharpens everything
jobCostGround.question: Which of these are part of the picture for you lately?
jobCostGround.hint: Up to 3, or skip. Always optional.

options.text: Anxiety
Low mood
Focus / ADHD-type struggles
Sleep problems
Loneliness
Social anxiety
Body image or eating stuff
Perfectionism
Prefer not to say

fallbackFollowup.kicker: One more, while we're being honest
fallbackFollowup.question: Imagine a week where it simply wasn't available — server down, app gone. What's the first feeling, before the reasonable thoughts arrive?

options.text: Relief. Which probably says a lot
Low-grade panic about what's happening without me
A boredom I wouldn't know what to do with
Loneliness, honestly
Untethered — like I'd lost the place I go to feel okay
Nothing much. I'd adapt
